title: Hybrid-precision kernel router with profile-led calibration and accuracy validation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As we onboard FP8/INT8 profiles alongside existing FP16 variants, the runtime needs a robust, testable kernel routing layer that selects the optimal execution path per-request while preserving model quality and SLOs. Current heuristics are statically mapped to model families and do not consider per-profile calibration statistics or recent accuracy regressions. This ticket proposes a profile-driven hybrid-precision kernel router plus a CI-backed calibration & accuracy validation workflow.
goals: 1) Build a runtime router that can choose FP16 / FP8 / INT8 kernels at module granularity using quantization profile metadata and live calibration stats. 2) Integrate a calibration pipeline that produces per-model, per-layer numeric summaries (scale ranges, clipping points, activation histograms) stored with the profile. 3) Add automated accuracy validation (eval suites) per-profile before enabling a profile in production routing. 4) Expose telemetry and safety fallback logic to meet latency and quality SLOs.
proposed_design:
- Profile format: extend quant profiles to include layer-level aggregate stats (mean, std, min/max, percentile ranges) and a conservative quality score. Profiles are JSONL with a version tag; compat layer for older profiles.
- Router policy: priority-order resolution: explicit request override -> model pin -> profile score threshold -> latency-sensitive fast path. Router computes expected token latency delta and estimated quality impact using stored metadata.
- Granularity: default module-level decisions (embedding, FFN, attention), with optional per-layer directives for high-risk layers.
- Fallbacks: automatic rollback to FP16 if (a) observed top-1 metric drop > configured delta OR (b) tail latency crosses SLO.
- CI gating: when a new profile is generated, CI runs full-suite evals (regression test set + production-like prompts) and populates profile QA fields. Only profiles with QA pass flag are marked routable.
calibration_workflow:
1) Offline calibration job (dataset + quant config) writes raw histograms and scale factors to staging profiles. 2) Post-calibration validator transforms histograms into summary stats and runs fast bit-exact shadow runs against reference FP16 outputs to compute relative error distributions. 3) Profiles that meet pre-defined error thresholds are promoted to 'staging-routable' and queued for CI evals. 4) CI eval runs full accuracy & regression suites; results are attached to the profile and decide final promotion.
Artifacts: confluence: https://redwood.example.com/confluence/runtime/quant-profiles and GH job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/actions?query=calibration
acceptance_criteria: Router can evaluate at runtime and choose FP16/FP8/INT8 kernels based on a profile's QA score and latency estimate
Calibration pipeline emits profile JSONL with layer summaries and QA flags
CI evaluation automatically gates profile promotion and provides granular accuracy metrics (per-layer and global)
Telemetry surfaces per-request decision, estimated vs actual latency delta, and accuracy regression alerts to console-2025.02 dashboard
Safe fallback to FP16 is automatic on quality or latency regressions; incidents generate a playbook alert
tests_and_validation:
- Unit tests for profile parsing, router decision determinism, and fallback triggers.
- Integration tests: synthetic workloads that simulate high variance input distributions; assert correct fallback behavior.
- E2E CI job: new-profile -> calibration -> CI eval -> deploy to canary pool -> monitor metrics for 24h before wide rollout.
- Benchmarks: measure p50/p99 latency and token cost delta across small, medium, and large models; target <5% median latency increase for INT8 path compared to FP16 baseline when beneficial for cost.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal canary with non-critical customers (dedicated pools) for 48h. 2) Gradual enable via rollout policy: 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100%, with automatic halt on regression. 3) Post-rollout audit and add retraining jobs to calibration dataset if drift detected.
telemetry_and_observability: Emit events: profile_id, chosen_precision, computed_quality_score, estimated_latency_delta, observed_latency, fallback_reason. Dashboard widget: per-profile health, accuracy delta, traffic split, and recent CI evaluation history. Alerting: quality_regression_high and latency_sla_breach mapped to oncall and SEV process.
compatibility_and_migration: Router should accept legacy profiles (v1) by mapping missing layer-level stats to conservative defaults and marking them 'low-confidence'. Migration script provided to re-run legacy calibration jobs over common models to produce v2 profiles. Deprecation window: 6 months.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Risk: aggressive INT8/FP8 routing may cause subtle accuracy regressions on tail prompts. Mitigation: conservative QA thresholds, shadow traffic evaluation, and automatic rollback.
- Complexity: per-layer routing increases decision overhead; mitigate with caching of routing decisions for repeated model+prompt fingerprints.
- Storage: layer histograms increase profile size. Mitigation: store only summaries and drop full histograms after CI validation.
